task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of July 1, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Plain Bower Print's memorial-program work and the service decisions involved in small, time-sensitive orders.

facts.text: A June 2026 production note records Plain Bower Print setting aside a finished proof until the ordering family confirmed a name's spelling.
The four-person shop prints memorial programs, community notices and short-run event booklets in the town of Fernhollow.
Memorial orders commonly involve between 50 and 150 copies, according to the shop's job register for January 1 through June 30, 2026.
A standard 100-copy folded program package costs $90 and includes one proof and one ordinary correction round.
Additional pages, special paper and changes after printing begins are quoted separately rather than included in every order.
The shop asks for a written approval by email or on a paper proof before producing the full run.
A family can bring a handwritten draft and photographs; the shop charges separately when substantial scanning or layout work is required.
The register shows 42 memorial orders from January 1 through June 30, 2026, compared with 29 from July 1 through December 31, 2025.
Those figures describe the shop's workload and do not establish a change in local deaths or funeral attendance.
Owner Leda Norven says referrals from two local service organizers changed during that period.
Norven said, "The deadline is usually fixed before we see the first page, so the checking has to have its own place in the schedule."
Customer Oren Mallen, who organized a family memorial, chose a plain folded program so several relatives could review it without discussing a more elaborate design.
Mallen said, "The paper proof let us point to the same line instead of describing it over the phone."
The supplied customer account includes no deceased person's name, medical information or private family correspondence.
The shop retains approved production files for 30 days after the initial print run for agreed reprints, then deletes them under its stated retention policy.
A reprint uses the approved version unless a further correction is explicitly agreed; staff do not assume a later telephone message replaces the proof.
The shop has not supplied a profit breakdown separating memorial work from other short-run jobs.
Norven says rush work can displace less urgent printing, but the business does not promise to accept every same-day request.
The front counter retains a display of paper samples from the shop's former wedding-stationery business.
No claim is supplied that printed programs provide a particular emotional or therapeutic outcome for every family.

forbidden_additions: A rise in local deaths inferred from the order count or a guaranteed emotional outcome
Invented deceased identities, private messages or acceptance of every rush request
